Please note that this summary of our main maritime fees is drawn from formal legislation and is intended as a quick guide only.

For a full account of the MCA’s revised fees and the context in which they should be applied, please refer to the Statutory Instrument.

For further confirmation of the fees you can expect to pay for various services, please check with your local Maritime and Coastguard Agency contact.

Standard hourly survey fee

Our standard hourly rate will be increasing to £120 per hour from 13 November 2018 and then to £147 per hour from 13 November 2019.

Certificates and Examinations for Officers

Cancellation of application

1. Where an application for an examination covered under item 1 in the table below is cancelled after the fee has been paid, a refund must be made of—

(a) £152 in the case of cancellation before a notice of eligibility has been issued,

or

(b) £130 in the case of cancellation after a notice of eligibility has been issued.

Table of fees

Item Subject of fee Amount of fee

1 The assessment of an application for a Certificate of Competency, the practical oral part of the examination, and the issue of a Certificate once the qualifying conditions are met £220

2 Resitting an examination in relation to item 1 £159

3 An initial assessment for qualification as a marine Engineer Officer (merchant ship) £121

4 The replacement of a lost certificate £77

5 An application for a certificate not requiring an oral examination £77

6 The addition or removal of, or amendment to, an endorsement or tanker endorsement £73

7 An application for a certificate of continued proficiency and updating of knowledge £54

Certificates of Equivalent Competency

Withdrawal or rejection of application

Where an application in relation to item 2 in the table below is withdrawn or rejected after the prescribed fee has been paid on the grounds that the applicant does not meet the preliminary criteria for detailed assessment, £50 must be refunded.

Item Subject of fee Amount of fee

(a) standard of English; or

(b) knowledge of United Kingdom legal and administrative processes £86

Seamen’s Documents

Fees for issue of documents

The fee for the issue, or replacement, of a British Seaman’s Card or a discharge book is £55. If you request and receive premium service, a fee of £50 is payable in addition to the aggregate of the fees for documents issued on the same occasion.

Lost documents

No fee is payable in respect of a replacement British Seaman’s Card or discharge book where the document has been lost, destroyed or defaced through no fault of the holder.

Compulsory Insurance Certificates

The fee payable on an application for the issue of a certificate under section 164 of the Act (which relates to certificates of compulsory insurance against liability for pollution) is £31.

The fee payable on an application for the issue of a certificate under section 255N[footnote 8] of the Act (which relates to wreck removal insurance satisfying the requirements of the Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks 2007[footnote 9]) is £31.

Additional Charges (Waiting Time, Abortive Visits and Attendance at Unusual Hours)

Where an inspection is delayed or is disrupted during its course or a visit to carry out an inspection is abortive, a fee calculated at the standard hourly rate for the delay caused or time wasted is chargeable.

The fee is not chargeable where—

(a) the delay or time wasted is less than one hour in total or is due to circumstances over which the applicant has no control; or

(b) the person carrying out the inspection is reasonably able to perform other work in the vicinity for which a fee has been paid.

Where any part of an inspection is carried out between 6pm and 8am on a weekday night or at any time on a Saturday, an additional fee of £74 per hour is chargeable for that part.

Where any part of an inspection is carried out in Scotland at any time on a Sunday or a Bank Holiday, an additional fee calculated at the standard hourly rate is chargeable for that part.

Where any part of an inspection is carried out in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland at any time on a Sunday or a Bank Holiday, or on Good Friday or Christmas Day, an additional fee calculated at the standard hourly rate is chargeable for that part.

Only one additional fee is charged to cover attendance at unusual hours, if a part of an inspection covers two or more of the periods described above.

Waste Management

The fee for the Secretary of State’s consideration and, if appropriate, approval or re- approval of a waste management plan prepared and submitted by a harbour authority or terminal operator in respect of a harbour or terminal pursuant, as the case may be, to regulation 6(1) or (2) or 8(1) of the Merchant Shipping and Fishing Vessels (Port Waste Reception Facilities) Regulations 2003[footnote 10] (“the Regulations”) is charged at the standard hourly rate. The fee for the preparation by the Secretary of State of a waste management plan in respect of a harbour or terminal pursuant to regulation 9 of the Regulations is charged at the standard hourly rate.

The fee for the issue by the Secretary of State of an exemption in respect of a harbour authority or terminal operator pursuant to regulation 15(1) and (2) of the Regulations, or in respect of a ship pursuant to regulation 15(3) of the Regulations, is £147.

Strategic Ships

The fee for the issue by the Secretary of State of an exemption, pursuant to section 48 of the Act (power to exempt from manning requirements), from the requirements in regulation 3 of the Merchant Shipping (Officer Nationality) Regulations 1995[footnote 11] relating to a strategic ship is £250.
